text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Netanyahu threatens to use Israeli military in Palestinian self-rule areas if more violence breaks out.
- A quarter of a million people visit Cairo International Fair on its last day on Friday.

- Foreign Minister Moussa to arrive in India today for non-aligned nations ministers conference. Ministers to discuss obstacles in the way of the peace process and the future of the non-aligned movement.
- Russian parliament praises Egypt's role in the peace process and affirms its disappointment with Netanyahu's settlement policy.
- German bank report says Egyptian economy has achieved many positive results and ranks economy in a leading position among Middle East and Mediterranean economies.

- Public Enterprise Minister Ebeid says will deliver messages from Mubarak to leaders of the United Arab Emirates during his visit there. He says will discuss possibility of involvement of Abu Dhabi Fund in 70 projects worth $8.7 billion.
- 24,000 Egyptians in holy lands for pilgrimage.
- Administrative watchdog to look into files of Islamic banks and to see if there have been any wrongdoings.
- Second tranche of Gulf War compensation to arrive in three months.
- Israeli Defence Minister Mordechai says after meeting U.S. secretary of state that the United States did not ask Israel to stop settlement activity.
- Cairo criminal court to start trial on Wednesday of former public sector chief Habbak on charges of embezzlement.
